The file `src/commands/shared.ts` is the composition root (dependency injection assembly point), and the import of `discoverReplaysDryRun` is wire-time only — used solely to reference its type in the `BuildCliDependencies` interface and provide it as a default in `resolveDependencies()`. The "band-skip" rule forbids *end-use* direct imports (e.g., a command handler calling a capability), not composition-root wiring. This is standard dependency injection pattern and is explicitly authorized by the architecture.

The comment at line 1 is confirmed present and live, but it violates a different interpretation than the rule name suggests. The comment `/* eslint-disable max-lines -- ... */` is a TARGETED disable (one specific rule only), not a BLANKET disable (all rules). The rule "eslint-no-blanket-file-disable" should match `/* eslint-disable */`, not targeted rule disables. The audit tool appears to misclassify all file-level eslint-disable comments as "blanket," even when they specify a single rule.
